title: Which bin? (broken on purpose: rule paper-cup-soiled removed, rule receipt-as-paper added)

values.label: Paper box
values.hint: Cardboard and pizza boxes. A delivery box lined with foil or plastic has its own choice.

values.label: Insulated box
values.hint: A box lined with foil or plastic that will not come off

values.label: Newspapers, books
values.hint: Take plastic-coated paper (a coated flyer, for example) out first: it goes in the general waste bag. The rest goes out as paper.

conditions.question: Is there food or grease on it that rinsing will not remove?
conditions.help: Rinse it first if you can. Answer Yes only if it is still dirty after rinsing.

values.label: Small
values.hint: A few pieces that fit wrapped in a bag.

conditions.question: What kind of glass is it?

values.label: Bottle, jar or ordinary drinking glass
values.hint: Ordinary drinking glasses and beer mugs count as ordinary glass (moe-2018 FAQ p.22 (유리잔)).

values.label: Heat-resistant, crystal, ceramic or window glass
values.hint: Includes coated or coloured glass products, lighting glass and pottery (사기·도자기).

conditions.question: Is the paper cup coated on both sides?

values.label: Yes
values.hint: Both the inside and the outside have a coating.

conditions.question: Is it a colourless, see-through PET water or drink bottle?

values.label: No
values.hint: Coloured, or not a PET drink bottle.

outcomes.label: Paper
outcomes.detail: Put it out with paper recycling.

outcomes.label: Drink cartons
outcomes.detail: Put it in the carton-only collection bin. If there is no carton bin, tie the cartons together and put them out beside the paper.

outcomes.label: Glass bottles
outcomes.detail: Put it out with glass bottles.

outcomes.label: Cans
outcomes.detail: Put it out with metal cans.

outcomes.label: Clear PET bottles
outcomes.detail: Put it out as a clear PET bottle, separate from other plastics.

outcomes.label: Plastics
outcomes.detail: Put it out with plastic containers.

outcomes.label: Plastic film
outcomes.detail: Put it out with plastic film and bags, inside a clear or semi-clear bag.

outcomes.label: Battery collection box
outcomes.detail: Put it in a battery collection box at a collection point.

outcomes.label: Fluorescent lamp collection box
outcomes.detail: Put it in your district's fluorescent lamp collection container.

outcomes.label: General waste bag (종량제봉투)
outcomes.detail: Put it in the general waste bag, called a 종량제봉투 (jongnyangje-bongtu). It is the pay-as-you-throw bag.

outcomes.label: Special sack for non-combustibles (특수규격마대)
outcomes.detail: Put it in a special sack for non-combustible waste, called a 특수규격마대 (teuksu-gyugyeok madae). You buy the sack. Large items can also go out as bulky waste (대형폐기물).

outcomes.label: Ask your district office
outcomes.detail: The guides this app uses do not cover this case. Ask your district office (구청) before you put it out.

rules.note: Take off any plastic coating, tape, staples and foil, then fold the box. The source line is about cardboard boxes (골판지상자); this app applies it to every paper box, pizza boxes included.

The Ministry's guide lists a pizza box as paper, and only the inner paper soiled with grease goes in the general waste bag. This app extends that line to any paper box with food or grease that rinsing will not remove, and sends the whole box to the general waste bag.
A box with a foil or plastic lining that cannot be separated from the paper cannot be recycled as paper.
Keep it dry, flatten it, stack it and tie it into a bundle. Remove plastic covers and spiral bindings first.
The FAQ line is about a hand towel with dirt on it, which goes in the general waste bag. This app applies it to newspaper, books and flyers with food or dirt on them.
A paper cup coated on both sides cannot be recycled as paper.
Empty it, rinse it with water and press it flat. Put cups in a bag or tie them together.
Empty it, rinse it and let it dry. Use the carton-only bin. If there is none, tie the cartons together and put them out beside the paper.
The FAQ says a carton with a lot of residue (다량) goes in the general waste bag; this app applies it to any residue that rinsing will not remove.
Thermal paper receipts cannot be recycled as paper.
Empty it and rinse it. Deposit bottles (soju, beer) can go back to a shop.
If it still has dirt on it, wash it as clean as you can and put it out with glass bottles anyway.
Wrap the pieces in newspaper first, then put them in the general waste bag.
A large amount of broken glass goes in a special sack for non-combustibles (특수규격마대).

Heat-resistant, crystal, coated or coloured glass, window glass, lighting glass and ceramics go in a special sack (특수규격마대) or can be put out as bulky waste (대형폐기물). The source lists these kinds for the special sack without a broken/whole split, so the answer is the same whether or not the glass is broken.
Empty it and rinse it. Remove plastic lids and anything else that is not metal.
If it still has dirt on it, wash it as clean as you can and put it out with cans anyway.
Aluminium foil goes in the general waste bag.
Empty it, peel off the label, press it flat and close the cap. Put it out separately from other plastics.
If it still has dirt on it, wash it as clean as you can and put it out as PET anyway.
Empty it and rinse it. Remove the label and any parts made of another material.

If it still has dirt on it, wash it as clean as you can. The FAQ line is about a dirty plastic bottle and says to put it out as PET; this app applies the wash-first advice to bottles that are not colourless drink bottles and keeps them with plastics.
Empty it and rinse it. Remove the label and any parts made of another material.
Neither guide says what to do with a plastic container that still has food or grease on it after rinsing.
Empty it, rinse it, and put it out inside a clear or semi-clear bag.
Film or wrap that cannot be cleaned, such as snack and noodle wrappers, goes in the general waste bag.
Empty it, rinse it and remove labels.
Styrofoam with food on it, or with dirt that is hard to remove, goes in the general waste bag.
Take the battery out of the device. Put it in a battery collection box at a collection point.
Put it in your district's fluorescent lamp collection container.
A small amount of a broken lamp goes in the general waste bag.
A large amount of a broken lamp goes in a special sack for non-combustibles (특수규격마대).
WRONG ON PURPOSE: contradicts rule receipt (general waste). Added for the demo.
